where_suggestion_comes_from.rule_in_words: For each NEEDS_CORRECTION finding with code TICKER_NOT_FOUND whose row is in the template, the server asks Kimi (model kimi-k3) whether the symbol is a typo and may return one ticker; the same provider read then verifies that ticker, and only an exact FOUND match is attached to the finding as a suggestion that the page offers as Did you mean X?
where_suggestion_comes_from.what_it_calls: Kimi kimi-k3 through KimiAdvisory.call('check') (a typo question, not a similarity question); then the provider read /securities/securities_info through the broker port. The browser calls neither: the Kimi key is read by the resident session on the server.

why_timxx_got_none.verdict_class: READ, with two RUN checks on the existing harness and one constructed case
why_timxx_got_none.read: The only producer of a suggestion is the typo check. TIMXX is not a one-character or transposition slip of any ticker, so the check's answer is null, and with a null answer the verify step never runs (upload_suggestions.py:63-66). Kimi's real reply for TIMXX is not in this worktree and was not asked for (no live call), so the null is an inference from the prompt, not a measured reply.
why_timxx_got_none.even_if_kimi_proposed: Had Kimi proposed a ticker, the provider read would still decide. A money-market ticker the provider does not answer FOUND exact for is refused there (upload_suggestions.py:76-79). For a fund row the provider answers only if its own display id is the bare ticker (security_resolution.py:52-58, :108-115); otherwise that ticker is refused by name.
why_timxx_got_none.run_existing_harness: RUN: timeout 120 python -m pytest infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/ycharts/generate/tests/test_y4_check_gate.py -k anything_but -p no:cacheprovider -q -> '6 passed, 10 deselected' rc=0. The six cases are the null answer, the same ticker, an advisory failure, a provider that does not know the proposal, a gated feature, and a failing verify read. The fixtures use APPL, not TIMXX.
